landing.description: A virtual office for remote teams, in the browser. Walk around a pixel-art floor with your team and start a video call just by standing next to someone.
features: Screen sharing in calls and meetings

items.a: TinyFloor is a virtual office you walk around in. Your team appears as pixel-art characters on a shared 2D floor, and a call starts when you stand next to someone instead of when you click a meeting link.

items.q: How does proximity video chat work?
items.a: Walk up to someone and a call button appears next to them. A tap starts a call, and once you're talking you can turn on your camera or share your screen. Calls run over WebRTC through Cloudflare's network, so they connect on any office or home network, and they stay up until someone hangs up. For a group, join a meeting and your character walks into the meeting room.
Yes, for an office of up to 3 people, with everything included. After that, Pro is $29 a month for the whole team, not per person.

items.q: Do I need to install anything?
items.a: No. TinyFloor runs in the browser on desktop and mobile. Open your office's link and you are inside.

items.q: Do I need an account to join an office?
items.a: Yes, a free one. An office is private: teammates join through its invite link and sign in with Google or email. To look around first, the demo office needs only a name.

An office floor is only for its members, and nothing inside it is public or indexed by search engines. Calls are encrypted in transit by WebRTC, and your camera and microphone are only on during a call.

items.q: How is TinyFloor different from Zoom or Google Meet?
items.a: Zoom and Google Meet put everyone in one grid until the meeting ends. A TinyFloor office stays open all day, so you can see who's around, drift between conversations and talk to whoever you walk over to, without scheduling a call.

gather.title: The best Gather alternatives in 2026.
gather.subtitle: Gather (formerly Gather Town) ended its free plan in September 2025 and now charges for every member. Here are seven alternatives, compared on what a real team pays, what's free, and what each one is best at. We make TinyFloor, so it's listed first; everything else comes from each product's own pages.

faq.q: What is the best free Gather alternative?
faq.a: For a team of up to 10, SoWork's free plan fits the most people, with meetings capped at 30 minutes; WorkAdventure's fits 10 people online at once. TinyFloor is free for up to 3 with every feature included, and $29 a month for the whole team after that.

faq.q: What is the cheapest Gather alternative for a team of 10?
faq.a: TinyFloor, at $29 a month for the whole team. SoWork's Basic plan is $54 a month billed yearly for 10 members, and Gather is $120 billed yearly.

faq.q: Is there a Gather alternative that runs in the browser?
faq.a: Yes. TinyFloor, Kumospace and WorkAdventure run in the browser; Teamflow and Roam are desktop apps.

faq.q: Does Gather still have a free plan?
faq.a: No. Gather ended its free plan on September 15, 2025. It costs $15 a member a month, or $12 billed yearly, after a 30-day trial.

faq.q: Can I move my Gather office to another tool?
faq.a: TinyFloor can't import a Gather map: you start with a ready-made office and invite everyone with one link, which takes minutes. Check with any other tool before you plan a move.

faq.q: Is TinyFloor like Gather?
faq.a: Yes, in the way that matters day to day: a pixel-art office where you walk up to someone to talk and step into a room to meet. It doesn't let you design the office, and it has no recordings or transcripts.

standup.title: A virtual standup your team walks into.
standup.subtitle: No calendar link and no waiting room. At standup time your team walks into the meeting room, says what they're on, and walks back to work.

faq.q: How do I run a virtual standup?
faq.a: Pick a time, meet in the same place every day and keep it short. On TinyFloor the main meeting is always there: people walk in at the time and walk out when it's done.

faq.q: Does a daily standup cost extra?
faq.a: No. Meetings come with every plan, with nothing to count. A 15-minute standup every working day is about 5 hours a month.

faq.q: Can we do async standups instead?
faq.a: Yes. Many teams post updates in a channel and keep the meeting room for the days that need talking.

faq.q: Do people need their cameras on?
faq.a: No. Cameras are optional in every meeting, and anyone without one shows as a card that lights up when they talk.

onboarding.label: Remote onboarding

meta.title: Remote Onboarding for New Hires in a Virtual Office
meta.description: Help new hires settle in remotely: from their first day they can see the team, know who to ask and walk over to ask it.

onboarding.title: Remote onboarding where new hires can see who to ask.
onboarding.subtitle: The hardest part of starting remotely is not knowing who's around, or whether it's OK to ask. On TinyFloor the team is right there, and asking is a short walk.

faq.q: How do new hires join?
faq.a: With your office's invite link. They make a free account, choose a name and a character, and land on the floor.

faq.q: Does a new hire take a seat on the plan?
faq.a: Yes, everyone in the office is a member. Pro has room for the whole team.

faq.q: Can new hires catch up on chat?
faq.a: Yes. Channels keep their history, so a new person can read back through the conversations they join.

faq.q: Does it replace our onboarding docs?
faq.a: No. Keep your docs and checklists where they are. TinyFloor makes the people part easier: who's who, and how to ask.

watercooler.label: Virtual watercooler

meta.title: Virtual Watercooler for Remote Teams
meta.description: The small talk remote teams miss: run into teammates on the floor, chat in the lounge and see what everyone's listening to, in a virtual office for your team.

watercooler.title: A virtual watercooler that happens on its own.
watercooler.subtitle: Remote teams schedule social time because nothing happens by chance. On a shared floor you pass people, see who's around and stop to chat.

faq.q: What is a virtual watercooler?
faq.a: It's the informal chat a remote team misses from an office: running into people and talking about anything. On TinyFloor it happens on the floor instead of in a scheduled call.

faq.q: Do watercooler chats count against anything?
faq.a: No. Chats between two people never count, and meetings come with every plan.

faq.q: Can we listen to music together?
faq.a: Yes, with Spotify. Play music right in TinyFloor and it shows on your card, so teammates can listen too. A Jam keeps everyone on the same song, in Spotify.

faq.q: Is it only for social time?
faq.a: No. The same floor is where your team works all day; the watercooler is just the part between tasks.

engineering.label: Engineering teams

meta.title: Virtual Office for Remote Engineering Teams
meta.description: A virtual office for remote engineering teams: unblock each other fast, pair with screen sharing, run standups and keep focus time quiet.

engineering.title: A virtual office for remote engineering teams.
engineering.subtitle: Engineers need long stretches of focus and quick answers when they're stuck. TinyFloor gives you both: quiet by default, and a teammate a short walk away.

faq.q: Does TinyFloor connect to GitHub or Jira?
faq.a: No. TinyFloor is where you talk, not where the work is tracked. Share your screen to look at anything together.

faq.q: Is it good for pair programming?
faq.a: Yes. Walk up to a teammate, start a call and share your screen. Add a third person and it becomes a meeting.

faq.q: How big can an engineering team be?
faq.a: Pro is made for a small team, up to 15 people in one office. Larger organisations give each team an office of its own.

faq.q: Can we keep Slack?
faq.a: Yes. Plenty of teams keep Slack for messages and use TinyFloor for presence, calls and meetings.

design.label: Design teams

meta.title: Virtual Office for Remote Design Teams
meta.description: A virtual office for remote design teams: quick critiques with screen sharing, a shared whiteboard and a team you can see, all in the browser.

design.title: A virtual office for remote design teams.
design.subtitle: Design gets better with quick, honest feedback. On TinyFloor a critique is a walk across the floor, not a calendar invite.

faq.q: Does TinyFloor connect to Figma?
faq.a: No. Open Figma as usual and share your screen in a call or a meeting to look at it together.

faq.q: Is the whiteboard shared?
faq.a: Yes. Everyone in the office sees the same board, and what's drawn stays there for when people come back.

faq.q: How much does it cost?
faq.a: Free for up to 3 people. Pro is $29 a month for the whole team, not per person.

faq.q: Do we need to install anything?
faq.a: No. TinyFloor runs in the browser on desktop and mobile.

startups.label: Startups

meta.title: Virtual Office for Remote Startups
meta.description: A virtual office for remote startups: keep the speed of sitting together, for one price per office. Free for 3 people, then $29 a month for the whole team.

startups.title: A virtual office for remote startups.
startups.subtitle: Early teams move fast because everyone is in the same room. TinyFloor puts a remote startup back in one room, for one price per office, not per hire.

faq.q: How much does TinyFloor cost for a startup?
faq.a: Free for up to 3 people. Pro is $29 a month for the whole team, not per person.

faq.q: Can we cancel any time?
faq.a: Yes. A paid plan runs to the end of what you've paid for, then the office moves back to Free. Nothing is deleted.

faq.q: What happens when we outgrow one office?
faq.a: An office is made for a small team, up to 15 people. As you grow, give each team an office of its own.

faq.q: Do we need any IT setup?
faq.a: No. It runs in the browser: send the invite link and people sign in with Google or email.

agencies.label: Agencies

meta.title: Virtual Office for Remote Agencies
meta.description: A virtual office for remote agencies: see who's free to help, review work together on a shared screen and keep the studio feeling, wherever people work.

agencies.title: A virtual office for remote agencies.
agencies.subtitle: An agency runs on quick reviews and knowing who's free to help. TinyFloor gives a remote studio one floor where both happen without a meeting link.

faq.q: Can clients join our office?
faq.a: Offices are for members, and everyone joins with a free account through the invite link. For client calls, keep the meeting tool your clients already use.

faq.q: How many people can we have?
faq.a: Your whole team, up to 15 people on Pro, for one monthly price for the whole office.

faq.q: Can freelancers join?
faq.a: Yes. Freelancers join like anyone else through the invite link, and you can remove them from the office when a project ends.

faq.q: Does it work for creative reviews?
faq.a: Yes. Share your screen in a call or a meeting, and sketch on the whiteboard together.

meetingRoom.label: Virtual meeting room
meetingRoom.line: Walk in to meet, walk out to leave

meta.title: Virtual Meeting Room for Remote Teams
meta.description: A meeting room your team walks into: join and your character takes a place at the table, with cameras, screen sharing and no meeting link.

meetingRoom.title: A virtual meeting room down the hall.
meetingRoom.subtitle: Every office has a meeting room that's always there. Join a meeting and your character walks in; walk out and you've left. No links, no waiting room.

faq.q: How many people can join a meeting?
faq.a: Everyone in the office: up to 3 people on Free, and the whole team on Pro.

faq.q: Do meetings have a time limit?
faq.a: No. Meetings come with every plan, with no meter to watch.

faq.q: What happens when the hours run out?
faq.a: Meetings carry on with voice only until the 1st of the month. Calls between two people are never counted.

faq.q: Can we have more than one meeting at once?
faq.a: Yes. Besides the main meeting, anyone can start another with a name and ask people in.

teamChat.label: Team chat

meta.title: Team Chat Beside Your Virtual Office
meta.description: Channels, direct messages and reactions that stay, right beside your team's floor. Catch up from your phone without walking in.

teamChat.title: Team chat that sits beside the floor.
teamChat.subtitle: Every office has its own chat with channels, direct messages and reactions. Messages stay, so you can catch up from your phone without walking in.

faq.q: Does the chat keep history?
faq.a: Yes. Each channel keeps its most recent 5,000 messages, on every plan.

faq.q: Can I use the chat on my phone?
faq.a: Yes. Open TinyFloor in your phone's browser to read and reply, without walking onto the floor.

faq.q: Can I edit or unsend a message?
faq.a: Yes. Edit a message after you've sent it, or unsend it if it shouldn't be there. Edited messages say so.

faq.q: Does it replace Slack?
faq.a: For a small team it can. Others keep Slack for messages and use TinyFloor for presence, calls and meetings.

presence.label: Team presence
presence.line: Who's in, busy or in a call

meta.title: Team Presence and Status for Remote Teams
meta.description: See who's in, who's busy and who's in a call, at a glance on one floor, then walk right over. Team presence for remote teams.

presence.title: Team presence you can see at a glance.
presence.subtitle: Everyone has a desk and a status on the floor. You can tell who's free, who's heads down and who's already in a call, before you ask.

faq.q: What statuses are there?
faq.a: Available, busy and away. Your status shows next to your name on the floor and in the list of people.

faq.q: Does TinyFloor track activity?
faq.a: No. It shows who's on the floor and the status they choose. It doesn't report on anyone's activity.

faq.q: Can I see who's around from my phone?
faq.a: Yes. The list of people works in your phone's browser too.

faq.q: How much does it cost?
faq.a: Free for up to 3 people. Pro is $29 a month for the whole team, not per person.

whiteboard.label: Online whiteboard
whiteboard.line: A shared board on the wall

meta.title: Online Whiteboard in Your Team's Virtual Office
meta.description: A shared whiteboard on the wall of your virtual office, for the sketch that explains it. It stays there when people come back.

whiteboard.title: An online whiteboard on the office wall.
whiteboard.subtitle: Walk up to the whiteboard and draw. Everyone in the office sees the same board, and what's on it stays for next time.

faq.q: Is the whiteboard shared with the whole office?
faq.a: Yes. Everyone in the office sees the same board.

faq.q: Can we rub things out?
faq.a: Yes. Use the eraser, or clear the whole board when you are done.

faq.q: Does it replace Miro or FigJam?
faq.a: No. It's for quick sketches while you talk. Keep your design tools for bigger work.

faq.q: Is it on every plan?
faq.a: Yes. Every plan has every feature, the free one included.

about.intro: TinyFloor is a virtual office for remote teams: a shared floor in the browser where you can see who's around and walk over to talk.

why.title: Why we're building it
why.body: Remote work is good for focus, but it lost the small moments: a quick question, a hello in passing, knowing who's around. Video calls turned every conversation into a meeting. TinyFloor gives a team one place to be together, so talking is as easy as walking over.
